dorsal-hump-rasping-diy.summary: Home filing or striking of a nasal bump in hopes of a smoother, flatter bridge; surgeons perform hump reduction as an operation under anesthesia.

quick.overview:
Dorsal hump rasping is the do-it-yourself attempt to flatten a bump on the bridge of the nose by filing or striking it. The payoff people want is a straighter, smoother side profile without paying for surgery.

The idea is that repeated filing or impact reduces the bone and cartilage of the bump. Reference sources describe hump reduction only as part of rhinoplasty, where a surgeon reshapes the bump with instruments under anesthesia and the nose is then taped and splinted while it heals. No published study or reliable source describes a home method, and the wiki's sources do not document how common it is.
quick.how: Posters who discuss it describe working on the bump themselves at home, without a surgeon. No published routine or timeline exists. The surgical version it imitates is followed by a dressing and splint, and swelling can take a year or more to settle fully.
quick.risks: The nasal bones and cartilage support breathing as well as shape. Injury, infection, airway problems and an uneven result are general concerns with any trauma to the nose, and no study evaluates the home practice. Anyone wanting a lower bridge can ask a facial plastic surgeon about rhinoplasty.

angle.text: The goal is a flatter, smoother nasal bridge without surgery. People who try it file or strike the bump at home, expecting the bone to wear down. Surgical sources describe hump reduction only as a surgeon-performed procedure.

nasal-splint-after-rhinoplasty.summary: A rigid or semi-rigid cover, sometimes with internal stents, that holds a freshly reshaped nose still so the surgical result heals in place.

quick.overview:
A nasal splint is the protective cover placed over the nose after rhinoplasty. It keeps the newly reshaped bones and cartilage from moving, so the nose heals in the shape the surgeon created.

The splint and tape hold the nose still and shield it from pressure and knocks during early healing. Internal splints, such as silastic or resorbable types, support the septum or cartilage from inside and are used in septal and nasal surgery. Studies of splints and packing are mostly in that surgery and compare bleeding, comfort and complications.
quick.how: The surgical team applies the tape and splint at the end of the operation, and the dressing is usually removed about a week later. It is worn only during early healing and is not something people buy or fit themselves. Internal splints are placed and removed by the surgeon.
quick.risks: Reported issues include discomfort, bacterial colonization with internal splints and, in one study, respiratory distress with totally occlusive packing compared with splints or sutures. Percutaneous osteotomy scars have also been described after rhinoplasty. Any problems with fit or breathing go back to the surgical team.

angle.text: After rhinoplasty, a splint and tape hold the reshaped nose still so it heals in the shape the surgeon created. It is usually removed after about a week. Patients and forum posters discuss it as part of protecting the surgical result.

nasal-irrigation.summary: Saline rinsing of the nose to clear congestion and support easier nasal breathing, a routine linked to sleep and face habits.

quick.overview:
Nasal irrigation flushes the nasal passages with salt water to clear mucus and congestion. People interested in nasal breathing use it to keep the nose open, which some link to better sleep and to breathing habits that affect the face.

Saline passes in one nostril and out the other, moistening the lining and rinsing out mucus, allergens and debris. It is an established practice from Ayurvedic tradition and appears in guidelines as an adjunct for sinus and allergy symptoms. No study has looked at whether it changes how the nose looks.
quick.how: People use a neti pot, squeeze bottle or similar device with a saline solution, often as part of a daily or as-needed hygiene routine, especially during colds, allergy season or when the nose feels blocked. Relief from congestion is typically noticed within the same session.
quick.risks: Reviews describe irritation, stinging and nosebleeds as the usual side effects. Rare fatal infections, including amoeba infections, have followed use of untreated tap water, and health agencies advise sterile, distilled or boiled and cooled water and regular cleaning of the device.

angle.text: A saline rinse clears mucus and congestion so the nose breathes more easily, which people link to better sleep and face habits. It is an established hygiene and medical practice. No studies have looked at its effect on nose appearance.

lip-flip-botox.summary: Botox in the upper lip muscle rolls the lip outward so more pink shows, making a thin upper lip look fuller for a few months.

quick.overview:
A lip flip makes a thin upper lip look fuller by showing more pink lip, without adding any volume. People choose it as a low-commitment, reversible way to change lip proportions, with the change visible within days.

Small amounts of botulinum toxin relax part of the orbicularis oris muscle along the upper lip border, so the lip rolls slightly outward and upward. Published work consists of technique descriptions, case series and reviews, including a 2021 case series and a 2025 systematic review. Effects are described as lasting about three to four months.
quick.how: A clinician performs it as a short in-office procedure, and people repeat it when it wears off if they like the look. It is often discussed as a cheaper alternative to filler or surgery. The term lip flip is also used for a filler technique, so the method matters when comparing results.
quick.risks: It is an off-label use of botulinum toxin. Weakening muscles around the mouth can affect symmetry and functions such as sipping, speaking and smiling while it lasts, and published abstracts give no firm complication rates. Medical sources describe it as clinician-performed.

angle.text: A lip flip makes a thin upper lip look fuller by relaxing the muscle so the lip rolls out and shows more pink, with the change visible within days. Results are temporary and reversible. Support comes from small studies and case series.

lip-lift-bullhorn-subnasal.summary: Surgery that shortens a long philtrum by removing skin under the nose, showing more pink lip with a permanent change.

quick.overview:
A lip lift shortens the space between the nose and upper lip so the lip sits higher and more pink shows. People with a long philtrum choose it to improve upper-lip proportions, and the change is permanent once healed.

A strip of skin is removed under the nose, which raises the lip and exposes more vermilion. In the bullhorn or subnasal version the scar is hidden under the nose. Surgeons have published case series since the early 1980s, including a 1986 paper on 83 patients and a 28-year series of direct excision approaches.
quick.how: A plastic surgeon performs it as an operation, with variants differing in where the incision sits. Swelling settles over the following weeks, and the scar matures over months. In forums it is discussed alongside philtrum length, chin-to-philtrum ratio and midface proportions.
quick.risks: The change is permanent. Scarring is the main concern in the literature, and forum accounts mention swelling and results that differ from what was expected. Standard surgical risks such as infection and asymmetry apply.

angle.text: A lip lift is used by people with a long philtrum who want more pink lip showing and better upper-lip proportions. Skin removed under the nose shortens the philtrum, with a permanent change once healed. In the bullhorn version the scar sits under the nose. The literature is mainly surgical case series.

fat-grafting-lips.summary: Your own fat injected into the lips for added volume that lasts longer than temporary fillers, with some fat reabsorbed over time.

quick.overview:
Lip fat grafting adds volume with your own tissue, giving fuller lips once swelling settles. It is described as one of the better semi-permanent options, lasting longer than temporary fillers.

Fat is taken from elsewhere on the body, usually by liposuction, then processed and injected in small amounts into the lips. The fat that survives stays as lip volume. Some of it is reabsorbed, and weight change can alter the result. No lip-specific trials were found; one source gives one-year retention of roughly 50 to 70 percent and says repeat sessions are often needed, though that source is unverified.
quick.how: A surgeon performs it in stages of harvesting, processing and reinjection. People often have a touch-up session if some volume is lost. Swelling and bruising settle over a period of days to weeks before the final look appears.
quick.risks: Reported issues include swelling, bruising, lumps, scarring, uneven results and volume loss. The donor area also heals from the harvest. Results vary from person to person.

angle.text: Lip fat grafting adds lasting volume using the patient's own fat, with fuller lips visible once swelling settles. Some of the fat is reabsorbed over time, and repeat sessions are sometimes needed. It is described as one of the better semi-permanent options.

lip-implants-permalip-gore-tex.summary: Permanent solid inserts of Gore-Tex or silicone that add lasting lip volume and definition, with extrusion and migration as the main risks.

quick.overview:
Lip implants are solid strips or tubes placed in the lips for permanent added volume. People choose them for a fuller, more defined lip that does not need repeat treatments like filler.

The two materials most discussed are ePTFE (sold as Gore-Tex and similar products) and solid silicone (Permalip). The implant sits in or near the lip muscle and adds bulk, and ePTFE is porous so tissue grows into it. Reports date from the early 1990s, including a 2002 paper on a redesigned implant and a 2017 retrospective study of 100 women. Use has declined relative to fillers.
quick.how: A surgeon places the implant through a small incision, and the lips settle over the following weeks. People who want durable volume consider it alongside fillers and fat grafting. The implant stays in place unless it is removed.
quick.risks: Reported complications include infection, extrusion, migration, shrinkage and hardening in some patients. Removal may be required. Because it is permanent, changing the look later means another operation.

angle.text: Gore-Tex or silicone implants are chosen by people who want permanent lip volume, with a fuller, more defined lip visible after healing. They are discussed alongside fillers and fat grafting as the durable option. Published studies are mostly case series.

lip-reduction-surgery.summary: Surgery that trims tissue to make thick lips smaller and better balanced with the face, mostly described for medical conditions.

quick.overview:
Lip reduction removes tissue so very full lips become smaller and sit in better balance with the rest of the face. The smaller lips are visible once healed.

Strips of tissue are excised, usually from the inner lip, so the scar sits inside the mouth. The literature mostly covers it for medical conditions such as macrocheilia from vascular malformations, granulomatous cheilitis and Van der Woude syndrome. A 2000 series of 66 patients found lip reduction far less common than enlargement, and a 2007 technique called bikini lip reduction was described for hypertrophic lips.
quick.how: A surgeon performs it as an operation, with healing over a few weeks. Interest in the cosmetic version is small compared with lip enlargement, and it is reported in places where thinner lips are preferred.
quick.risks: The change is permanent. Scarring and asymmetry are general surgical concerns, and cosmetic-specific outcome data are scarce.

angle.text: Lip reduction is used by people who feel very full lips are out of balance with the rest of the face, with smaller lips visible after healing. The literature covers it mainly for medical conditions such as macrocheilia, with little cosmetic research.

v-y-advancement-vermilion-advancement.summary: Flap surgery that moves pink lip tissue toward the lip border to show more vermilion; mostly used for reconstruction.

quick.overview:
Vermilion advancement moves the pink lip tissue to rebuild or enlarge it, so more pink shows and the lip looks fuller. The repositioned lip is visible after healing.

Flaps of lip tissue are advanced toward the lip border. In the literature it is mostly a reconstructive method, for example modified Goldstein-type vermilion flaps after Mohs surgery for lip cancer. In cosmetic surgery it is discussed as a way to increase pink lip show, and a 1996 review of cosmetic lip surgery set out guidelines on Cupid's bow, upper lip length and projection.
quick.how: A surgeon performs it as an operation, with the incision placed according to the technique chosen. Healing takes a few weeks, and the scar matures over months. Cosmetic use is thinly documented.
quick.risks: Surgical scarring and asymmetry are general concerns, and cosmetic-specific outcome data are not published in the sources reviewed.

angle.text: Vermilion advancement is discussed as a way to increase pink lip show, and the repositioned lip is visible after healing. In the literature it is mostly a reconstructive method, for example after tumour removal, with little cosmetic research.

lip-blushing-cosmetic-tattoo.summary: A cosmetic tattoo that tints the lips semi-permanently for even color and a softer, defined border.

quick.overview:
Lip blushing is a cosmetic tattoo that gives the lips a soft, even tint. People with uneven or pale lip color use it as a longer-lasting alternative to tinted balm, which wears off quickly, and the tint is visible once healed.

Pigment is placed in the skin of the lips by tattooing, so the color does not wash off and fades gradually. Cosmetic tattooing dates to the early twentieth century, with lip tattooing described as a fashion since the early 1930s. No trials have measured its effect on appearance, and the published literature is mainly case reports and reviews of complications.
quick.how: A tattoo or permanent makeup artist applies it in a session, with the color settling as the lips heal. People often have a touch-up later as it fades. Forum posters also mention cost and the possibility of an artificial look.
quick.risks: Reported problems include allergic and granulomatous reactions, infection risk with unsterile equipment, a case of squamous cell carcinomas arising in a lip tattoo, and difficult removal. Choosing a licensed, hygienic provider matters.

angle.text: Lip blushing is used as a semi-permanent alternative to tinted lip balm by people who describe their lip color as uneven or pale. Pigment placed in the lip skin gives an even tint and softer border once healed. Documentation is mostly case reports of reactions, with no appearance trials.

lip-liner-overlining.summary: Drawing liner just outside the natural lip line to make lips look fuller and more defined, a long-standing makeup technique with an instant result.

quick.overview:
Overlining makes lips look larger and more defined by tracing a lip pencil slightly beyond the natural lip edge. The fuller look is visible immediately, with no procedure.

The pencil extends the visible lip border and sharpens the contrast between lips and surrounding skin, so the lips look more prominent. Lip liner has been used since the 1920s, and makeup guidance describes overlining as a non-invasive way to suggest volume for people with thinner lips. No clinical studies measure its effect on perceived lip size or attractiveness.
quick.how: People draw the liner just beyond the lip line and fill the space with lip color, often blending the edge so it looks natural. It can be done daily and removed at the end of the day.
quick.risks: Pencils wash off, but allergic contact reactions to ingredients in lip products have been reported. Permanent lip-liner tattoos are a separate practice with documented complications and difficult removal.

angle.text: People draw liner just beyond the natural lip line and fill it in so lips look fuller and more defined, with the change visible immediately. It is a long-standing makeup technique, and its effect is seen directly rather than trial-tested.

plumping-gloss-menthol-cinnamon.summary: Tingling glosses that swell the lips briefly for a fuller pout without filler.

quick.overview:
Plumping glosses give a short-lived, visibly fuller pout without filler. People use them for a quick boost before a photo or night out.

The active ingredients mildly irritate the lip skin, which causes temporary swelling and a tingling or warming feeling. Wikipedia names capsaicin, the compound in chili peppers, as one such ingredient, and menthol and cinnamon are other common ones. The swelling fades within a short time, and no clinical studies of these glosses were found.
quick.how: People apply the gloss like an ordinary lip product, alone or over lipstick, and reapply for the effect. Results appear within minutes and last a few hours at most.
quick.risks: Because the mechanism is irritation, redness, stinging or discomfort can be expected, and people with sensitive lips or allergies to the ingredients may react more strongly. No studies of adverse events specific to these products were found.

angle.text: Users apply tingling menthol or cinnamon glosses to get a short-lived, visibly fuller pout without filler. Mild irritation causes the lips to swell, and the effect fades. Little formal research covers these specific ingredients.

lip-scrub-exfoliation.summary: A sugar or salt scrub that clears flaky skin so lips look smoother and take balm or color more evenly.

quick.overview:
A lip scrub rubs flaking skin off the lips so they look smoother and take balm or lipstick more evenly. The smoothing is visible right away.

Sugar or salt grains physically remove surface skin cells, which is a form of mechanical exfoliation. No studies of lip scrubs specifically were found. Dermatologists quoted on Wikipedia say exfoliation is not medically necessary because skin sheds on its own, and that lip licking and weather are common causes of chapping.
quick.how: People rub the scrub gently over the lips, rinse or wipe it off, and follow with balm or petroleum jelly. It is commonly done before applying lip color, and some do it once or twice a week.
quick.risks: Dermatologists quoted on Wikipedia say over-exfoliating can weaken the skin barrier and cause redness and sensitivity. Rough scrubbing on already cracked lips can cause irritation.

angle.text: Users rub on sugar or salt scrubs to clear flaking skin so lips look smoother and take balm or color more evenly. The smoothing is visible right away. No studies test lip scrubs specifically.

lip-balm-petrolatum-slugging.summary: Occlusive balm or petrolatum that seals in moisture so lips stay soft, smooth and less chapped.

quick.overview:
Lip balm and petrolatum keep lips soft, less cracked and less flaky, so they look smoother and healthier. It is routine lip care and the usual first-line approach for chapped lips.

Waxes and petrolatum are occlusives that slow water loss from the lip surface, while oils and butters soften it. Dermatology references describe simple chapped lips as usually responding to barrier lubricants such as balm or petroleum jelly. Applying a thick layer overnight is called slugging in skincare culture. Appearance trials are not a focus of research.
quick.how: People apply balm through the day and a thick layer of petrolatum at night. It pairs with avoiding lip licking and with sun-protective balms outdoors. Chapped lips often improve within a few days of consistent use.
quick.risks: Contact allergy to ingredients such as beeswax, propolis, carnauba wax and peppermint oil is documented. Petroleum jelly can contain mineral oil hydrocarbons, which a German consumer group flagged in 2015.

angle.text: Users apply balm or a thick layer of petrolatum to seal in moisture, keeping lips soft, less cracked and less flaky. It is routine lip care with a documented barrier effect, and appearance trials on it are not a focus of research.

lip-mask-overnight.summary: A thick occlusive treatment worn overnight so lips wake up softer and smoother.

quick.overview:
An overnight lip mask is a heavy lip product worn during sleep so lips are softer and smoother by morning. It works like a thick lip balm.

Occlusive ingredients such as petrolatum and lanolin slow water loss from the lips, and thicker emollients give longer moisture retention. Medical-grade lanolin is noted by Wikipedia to speed healing of chapped lips. No studies of products marketed as lip masks were found.
quick.how: People apply a layer before bed and wipe or wash it off in the morning, often after a gentle exfoliation. It is part of a night-time skincare routine, with softer lips noticeable by the next morning.
quick.risks: Allergic reactions to ingredients such as beeswax and propolis have been reported. Anyone allergic to lanolin or a listed ingredient can check labels before use.

angle.text: Users leave a rich lip mask on during sleep to wake with softer, smoother lips. It sits in the same family as balm and petroleum jelly, whose barrier effect is documented. Appearance-specific trials are lacking.

shot-glass-lip-challenge.summary: A viral suction trick that swells the lips briefly for a fuller look; bruising is the commonly reported result.

quick.overview:
The shot glass lip challenge uses suction from a small glass pressed over the mouth to make the lips swell and look fuller for a short while. It spread as a social-media trend as a no-cost version of lip plumping.

The suction draws blood into the lip tissue, producing short-lived swelling rather than any lasting change to lip structure. Medical sources describe suction plumping as causing temporary swelling. No clinical studies have tested the trend itself.
quick.how: People press the rim of a small glass over their mouth, create suction and hold it briefly, then take it off to see the effect. The fuller look fades within hours.
quick.risks: Bruising and swelling are the commonly reported effects, and clinical references on lip augmentation list irritation, bleeding and uneven lips among possible effects. There is no regulatory or clinical guidance specific to the trend.

angle.text: People press a small glass over the mouth to create suction for a quick, visibly fuller look. Suction draws blood into the lips and the swelling is short-lived. It is a DIY version of suction plumping, and no studies of the trend exist.

tinted-lip-balm-for-men.summary: Moisturizing balm with a sheer wash of color that evens lip tone for a healthier look without obvious makeup.

quick.overview:
Tinted lip balm gives lips a healthier, more even tone without the opacity of lipstick. Men use it as a low-key grooming step, and the color is visible on application.

Sheer pigments are mixed into a wax, butter and oil base that coats the lips, adding color while reducing moisture loss. Product descriptions emphasize hydration, a lightweight texture and a natural finish. No studies have tested tinted balms for appearance in men.
quick.how: People apply it like ordinary lip balm, building the color with more layers if they want it stronger. It fits into a daily routine and needs no special technique.
quick.risks: It is generally a low-risk cosmetic. Dermatologists note some ingredients and fragrances can irritate sensitive lips.

angle.text: Men use tinted balm for a subtly healthier, more even lip tone without the opacity of lipstick. The color change is visible on application. It is a low-key grooming product with no appearance trials.

hyaluron-pen-needle-free.summary: A high-pressure needle-free injector sold for at-home lip filler; the FDA has warned against it and a survey reports frequent complications.

quick.overview:
The hyaluron pen is promoted online as a way to get fuller lips from hyaluronic acid filler at home without needles. Marketing also mentions wrinkles.

The handheld device uses compressed air or a spring to force a jet of filler through the skin surface, with depth and amount depending on pressure and technique. Results and delivery depth are anecdotal. The US FDA issued a safety communication in October 2021 stating that needle-free devices have not been approved or evaluated for injecting dermal fillers, lack control over where filler goes and have been associated with serious injuries.
quick.how: It is sold to consumers for home use, with users pressing the pen against the lips to push the filler in. Professionals using filler for lips typically use needles or cannulas in a clinic.
quick.risks: Reported problems include infection, lumps, scarring, vascular occlusion with tissue death and permanent damage. A population-based survey of users and injectors reported complications in about 79 percent of respondents, and a 2022 paper in Dermatologic Surgery described DIY hyaluron pen content on social media as a safety threat.

angle.text: Users promote the pen as a way to get lip filler at home without needles, with pressure pushing filler through the skin into the lips. The claimed results and delivery depth are anecdotal, and the FDA has issued warnings about the device.

lip-hydration-water-intake.summary: Drinking water and humidifying indoor air to keep lips smoother and less dry.

quick.overview:
Drinking enough water and humidifying indoor air is a habit people use to keep lips from drying out, so they look smoother and less cracked.

The vermilion lip loses water easily because its outer layer is thin, so more moisture in the body or the air is thought to help the surface stay soft. Research on drinking water and lip texture is thin. One 2014 study of 22 women examined how lip hydration affects tactile and thermal sensitivity, not appearance.
quick.how: People drink water through the day, run a humidifier in dry rooms or while sleeping, and combine this with balm. It costs little and fits into an ordinary routine.
quick.risks: No risks are documented for the habit itself. Persistent dryness or cracking can have other causes, and a doctor can check it.

angle.text: Users drink more water and humidify indoor air to cut moisture loss and keep lips smoother and less dry. The lip's thin outer layer loses water easily, though the effect of drinking water on lip appearance has not been tested directly.

lip-microneedling.summary: Fine needling of the lips aimed at softer lines and a little extra volume through collagen induction.

quick.overview:
Lip microneedling is used to soften fine lines around the lips and add modest fullness. Proponents aim for smoother, slightly plumper lips without filler.

Tiny sterile needles puncture the skin, which is thought to trigger repair and collagen production. Microneedling is used for scarring and acne elsewhere on the face, and research on it is described as ongoing. No studies specific to the lips were found.
quick.how: A provider performs it in sessions, often as a series, with results building over weeks as the skin repairs. It is sometimes combined with other skin treatments.
quick.risks: Infection is the key concern, particularly with unregulated providers. A 2024 CDC report linked HIV cases to a spa microneedling facial. Redness and swelling after a session are expected.

angle.text: Proponents use microneedling on the lips to soften fine lines and add modest volume through collagen induction. Tiny punctures trigger skin repair. The technique is established for scars elsewhere on the face, and no lip-specific studies were found.
